explain.say: When you turn on a tap, clean water comes out. But it may have started in a muddy river or lake! How is it cleaned? Look at the board. First, metal screens catch big bits, like leaves, twigs and plastic.

explain.say: See the settling tanks? The water rests, and heavy mud and grit sink to the bottom. This is called sedimentation. Sometimes a chemical is added to clump tiny bits together so they sink faster. Is the water safe yet, do you think?

explain.say: Not yet! Look at the filters. The water trickles slowly through beds of sand and gravel, which trap even smaller bits. Now it looks clear. But clear does not mean safe. What tiny invisible things do you think might still be there?

explain.say: Germs! Look at this step. A small amount of chlorine is added, which kills bacteria and other microbes. Some places use ozone or ultraviolet light too. That is why tap water can smell a tiny bit like a swimming pool. Have you noticed that?

explain.say: Brilliant! Look at the board: each step removes something different. Wow: before cities cleaned their water, diseases like cholera spread through it. In London in 1854, Dr John Snow traced a cholera outbreak to one water pump. Next time you drink tap water, you will know its journey!

faq.a: Sedimentation is letting water stand in big tanks so heavy particles like mud and grit sink to the bottom.
asks: Why does water sit in settling tanks?

faq.q: How do sand filters clean water?
faq.a: As water trickles through layers of sand and gravel, small particles get stuck in the gaps, so cleaner water comes out below.
asks: What does filtration do in water treatment?

faq.q: Why is chlorine added to water?
faq.a: Chlorine kills bacteria and other microbes that could cause diseases like cholera and typhoid. Only a tiny, safe amount is used.
asks: Is chlorine in tap water safe?

faq.a: Potable water is water that is safe to drink. It is not pure water, because it still has some dissolved minerals, but it has no harmful amounts of germs or chemicals.

faq.q: How do countries with little fresh water get drinking water?
faq.a: Some, like Saudi Arabia, Israel and Singapore, use desalination: removing salt from seawater by distillation or by forcing it through very fine membranes, called reverse osmosis.

facts: Typical water treatment includes screening, sedimentation, filtration and disinfection with chlorine, ozone or ultraviolet light.
In 1854 John Snow linked a London cholera outbreak to a contaminated water pump on Broad Street.
